ui_ux_improvements.title: Add visible focus indicators for keyboard navigation
ui_ux_improvements.description: Replace focus:outline-none with visible focus rings on interactive elements across the app to improve keyboard accessibility and WCAG compliance.
ui_ux_improvements.rationale: Analysis found 107 instances of 'focus:outline-none' across 55 files, with many buttons and inputs removing focus indicators without providing visible alternatives. This creates accessibility barriers for keyboard users and fails WCAG 2.1 Success Criterion 2.4.7 (Focus Visible). The app already has good patterns in some components (PlatformCard.tsx uses focus:ring-2 focus:ring-sky-500/50) but this isn't consistent.
ui_ux_improvements.current_state: ChatInput.tsx (line 93) has 'focus:outline-none focus:border-white/20' which removes the default focus ring with only a subtle border change. GenerativeSidebar.tsx textarea (line 395) has 'focus:border-pink-500 focus:ring-2' which is good. SettingsModal.tsx inputs (9 occurrences) use focus:outline-none. Many buttons across the app use 'focus:outline-none' without replacement focus indicators.
ui_ux_improvements.proposed_change: Create a standardized focus utility class in Tailwind config or styles.ts: 'focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-yellow-400/50 focus-visible:ring-offset-2 focus-visible:ring-offset-stone-950 focus:outline-none'. Use focus-visible (not focus) to only show for keyboard navigation. Apply to all buttons, inputs, links. Add to PlatformCard pattern as standard. For high-contrast mode, add 'contrast-more:focus-visible:ring-current contrast-more:focus-visible:ring-offset-0' as fallback per Design System Section 3.2.
ui_ux_improvements.user_benefit: Keyboard users can clearly see which element is focused while navigating. Screen reader users get proper focus management. App becomes WCAG 2.1 AA compliant for focus visibility. Power users who prefer keyboard navigation have better experience.

ui_ux_improvements.title: Redesign ErrorBoundary with branded error page
ui_ux_improvements.description: Transform the basic ErrorBoundary fallback UI from stark white/red text to a polished, on-brand error recovery screen with retry options and support links.
ui_ux_improvements.rationale: The current ErrorBoundary.tsx (lines 30-40) renders a jarring white background with red text that breaks the dark theme experience. When errors occur, users see 'Something went wrong' with raw error details - this looks broken and unprofessional. Error states are critical UX moments that can either frustrate users or build trust through graceful handling.
ui_ux_improvements.current_state: ErrorBoundary.tsx line 32 shows: 'p-5 text-red-600 bg-white' with raw error stack traces in a <details> element. This creates visual whiplash from the dark app theme. No recovery actions are offered. Error details are shown raw without explanation. The component lacks role='alert' aria attributes.
ui_ux_improvements.proposed_change: Redesign the fallback UI: (1) Use dark theme colors (bg-stone-950 text-white) matching the app, (2) Add Signal-branded error illustration or icon (existing material-icons: error_outline), (3) Show user-friendly message: 'Something unexpected happened' with 'We've logged this issue and are looking into it', (4) Add 'Try Again' button that calls window.location.reload(), (5) Add 'Go to Dashboard' button, (6) Add 'Report Issue' link to support, (7) Collapse technical details into an expandable section for debugging, (8) Add role='alert' aria-live='assertive' for screen readers. Style buttons with existing BTN_NEU_SOLID patterns.
ui_ux_improvements.user_benefit: Errors feel handled rather than catastrophic. Users have clear recovery paths instead of being stuck. Consistent dark theme maintains immersion. Technical details available for debugging without overwhelming regular users. Professional error handling builds trust in the app.

ui_ux_improvements.title: Add swipe-to-dismiss gesture for mobile GenerativeSidebar bottom sheet
ui_ux_improvements.description: Implement native-feeling swipe-down gesture to dismiss the mobile AI Studio bottom sheet, matching iOS/Android system sheet behaviors.
ui_ux_improvements.rationale: GenerativeSidebar.tsx (lines 587-651) renders as a bottom sheet on mobile with a drag handle indicator (line 593: 'w-10 h-1 bg-zinc-700 rounded-full') but swiping down doesn't dismiss it - users must tap the X button. Mobile users expect bottom sheets to be swipe-dismissible based on iOS/Android system behaviors. The drag handle visual suggests swipe functionality that doesn't exist.
ui_ux_improvements.current_state: Mobile bottom sheet has visual drag handle but no gesture support. Close requires tapping the small X button (line 596-599). The sheet has max-h-[80vh] but no dynamic height based on swipe. The drag handle indicator is decorative only. Touch targets are good (min-w-[40px] min-h-[40px]) but the primary dismissal UX is suboptimal.
ui_ux_improvements.proposed_change: Add swipe-to-dismiss using touch events or a lightweight library: (1) Track touchstart/touchmove/touchend on the header area, (2) If user swipes down > 100px from drag handle, trigger dismiss with spring animation, (3) Add visual feedback during drag (sheet follows finger), (4) Add velocity-based dismiss (fast swipe triggers close), (5) Add partial drag state where sheet snaps back if swipe < threshold, (6) Use will-change: transform for 60fps performance per Design System Section 7.2. Can implement with pure JS or use existing useSpring hook pattern from AppShell.tsx.
ui_ux_improvements.user_benefit: Mobile users can dismiss the sidebar naturally with one-handed swipe gesture. Reduces accidental taps on small close button. Matches user mental model from other apps. Faster workflow on mobile. The drag handle becomes functional, not just decorative.

ui_ux_improvements.title: Add descriptive alt text to PlatformCard images for screen readers
ui_ux_improvements.description: Replace empty alt attributes on platform card images with descriptive text that conveys the platform identity to screen reader users.
ui_ux_improvements.rationale: PlatformCard.tsx line 136 has alt='' on the 3D platform images. While the button has focus styling and the Icon component provides some context, screen reader users navigating the dashboard hear only the button text without understanding the visual representation. WCAG 1.1.1 requires meaningful alt text or proper aria-hidden treatment.
ui_ux_improvements.current_state: PlatformCard.tsx line 136: . The empty alt tells screen readers to ignore the image, but the image is decorative AND informative (it shows the platform logo). The surrounding button only contains Icon + platform name + description. A blind user would understand 'LinkedIn Professional' but miss the visual branding context that sighted users get from the 3D images.
ui_ux_improvements.proposed_change: Update alt text to be descriptive: alt={`${config.name} logo - 3D illustration`}. This provides: (1) Platform identity confirmation, (2) Image type context (3D illustration), (3) Richer browsing experience for screen reader users. Alternatively, use aria-hidden='true' on the image if we consider it purely decorative AND add aria-label to the button: aria-label={`Create content for ${config.name} - ${config.description}`}. Also add role='img' for semantic clarity.
ui_ux_improvements.user_benefit: Screen reader users get complete information about each platform card. Blind users understand the visual design language of the app. WCAG 1.1.1 compliance improves. More inclusive experience for users with visual impairments.

ui_ux_improvements.title: Standardize skeleton loader styles with shimmer animation
ui_ux_improvements.description: Unify all skeleton loading states to use the shimmer variant consistently for a more polished perceived-performance experience.
ui_ux_improvements.rationale: Skeleton.tsx defines both 'rect' (animate-pulse bg-white/5) and 'shimmer' (uses .skeleton CSS class) variants. Analysis shows inconsistent usage: App.tsx line 684 uses <Skeleton height={200}> (defaults to rect), while DashboardPage line 326 also uses non-shimmer. The shimmer effect creates a more premium loading experience that matches the Life OS Design System's luxury aesthetic.
ui_ux_improvements.current_state: Skeleton.tsx (lines 25-27) defaults to 'rect' variant with animate-pulse. The 'shimmer' variant exists but requires explicit variant='shimmer'. Throughout the app, skeleton usages like App.tsx lines 656-665, 673, 683-685 all use default rect variant. The ImageCardSkeleton (Skeleton.tsx lines 49-58) also uses default non-shimmer. This creates inconsistent loading experiences across different views.
ui_ux_improvements.proposed_change: Update Skeleton component: (1) Change default variant from 'rect' to 'shimmer' in Skeleton.tsx line 16, (2) Ensure .skeleton CSS class in index.css has performant shimmer animation (linear gradient moving left-to-right), (3) Add variant='pulse' as explicit option for cases where shimmer isn't wanted, (4) Update ImageCardSkeleton to use shimmer, (5) Verify shimmer respects prefers-reduced-motion via CSS. The shimmer animation should be subtle (10-20% opacity variation) not flashy.
ui_ux_improvements.user_benefit: Consistent, premium-feeling loading states across all views. Shimmer effect provides better perceived performance by suggesting content is 'streaming in'. Cohesive design language reinforces app quality. Reduced cognitive load from consistent patterns.

ui_ux_improvements.title: Add Toast Notification Auto-Dismiss Progress Indicator
ui_ux_improvements.description: Add a visual progress bar at the bottom of toast notifications showing remaining time before auto-dismiss, pausing when user hovers.
ui_ux_improvements.rationale: Toast.tsx implements pause/resume on hover via ToastContext but users have no visual feedback about when notifications will disappear. This creates uncertainty - users can't tell if they have time to read the message. A shrinking progress bar creates predictability and leverages the existing hover-pause functionality.
ui_ux_improvements.current_state: Toast.tsx (lines 143-155) calls pauseToast/resumeToast on hover but this is invisible to users. The toast duration is configurable but not visualized. Users cannot see that hovering pauses the timer. The component uses transform-based animations which is good for performance.
ui_ux_improvements.proposed_change: Add a thin progress bar: (1) Create new div at bottom of toast: className='absolute bottom-0 left-0 h-0.5 origin-left' (2) Add CSS animation: @keyframes toast-progress { from { transform: scaleX(1) } to { transform: scaleX(0) } } (3) Set animation-duration to match toast.duration (4) Pause animation on hover via animation-play-state: paused (5) Use brand colors per toast type (orange for info/success, red for error) (6) Add motion-reduce:hidden for accessibility. Implementation: style={{ animationDuration: `${toast.duration}ms`, animationPlayState: isPaused ? 'paused' : 'running' }}
ui_ux_improvements.user_benefit: Users gain visual certainty about notification timing. The hover-pause feature becomes discoverable. Reduces notification anxiety especially for error messages. Creates a more polished, professional interaction pattern.

ui_ux_improvements.title: Increase MainNav Active State Visual Contrast
ui_ux_improvements.description: Strengthen the visual distinction between active and inactive navigation items by increasing indicator width, background opacity, and adding aria-current attribute.
ui_ux_improvements.rationale: MainNav.tsx uses a 1px-wide yellow bar (line 94-103) and subtle 12% opacity background for active state. This provides insufficient contrast ratio for users with color vision deficiencies (8% of males). The hover arrow starts at opacity: 0 making the affordance invisible. WCAG requires 3:1 contrast for state indicators.
ui_ux_improvements.current_state: MainNav.tsx line 94 sets active indicator height to 24px but width is only w-1 (4px). Line 83-86 shows active background is rgba(250, 204, 21, 0.12) which is barely visible. The ArrowRight indicator (lines 134-142) starts at opacity: 0, wasting the affordance.
ui_ux_improvements.proposed_change: Increase visual weight: (1) Change indicator width from w-1 to w-1.5 (6px) on line 93 (2) Increase active background opacity from 0.12 to 0.20 on line 84 (3) Add fontWeight: 700 for active text (currently 600) on line 127 (4) Set arrow initial opacity to 0.3 instead of 0 on line 137 (5) Add aria-current='page' to active button for screen readers (6) Add optional left-side highlight effect for redundant encoding
ui_ux_improvements.user_benefit: Users immediately identify their current location without relying solely on color. Color blind users can navigate confidently. Screen readers announce current page. The nav becomes usable by a wider range of abilities and preferences.

ui_ux_improvements.title: Add Dashboard Loading Skeleton with Content Structure Preview
ui_ux_improvements.description: Replace the simple spinner fallback in App.tsx with a content-aware skeleton that mirrors the dashboard layout structure during initial load.
ui_ux_improvements.rationale: App.tsx lines 411-420 show a Suspense fallback with just a spinning icon and 'Loading Signal...' text. This provides no spatial preview of upcoming content. Research shows skeleton screens improve perceived performance by 10-20% by showing layout structure immediately.
ui_ux_improvements.current_state: App.tsx DashboardPage fallback (lines 411-420) shows: 'Loading Signal...' with spinning dashboard icon. Meanwhile, the existing Skeleton component with shimmer variant is available but unused here. Users see a minimal loader then sudden content pop-in which feels jarring.
ui_ux_improvements.proposed_change: Create DashboardSkeleton component: (1) New file: src/components/dashboard/DashboardSkeleton.tsx (2) Mirror grid layout: 2x3 grid of PlatformCard skeletons (3) Include header skeleton with user menu placeholder (4) Show recent designs section skeleton (5) Use existing <Skeleton variant='shimmer' /> (6) Match spacing/padding of actual dashboard. Replace App.tsx fallback with <DashboardSkeleton />. Add aria-busy='true' aria-label='Loading dashboard' for accessibility.
ui_ux_improvements.user_benefit: Dashboard appears to load instantly with structure preview. Users understand what's coming before content renders. Perceived performance improves significantly. Creates a premium, polished first impression.

ui_ux_improvements.title: Animate EmptyState Illustration with Brand Colors
ui_ux_improvements.description: Transform the static gray EmptyState icon into an animated, on-brand illustration using the Signal Design System's orange/emerald palette.
ui_ux_improvements.rationale: EmptyState.tsx uses text-zinc-600 for the icon and sky-500/teal-500 for the CTA button - violating the Anti-Slop color guidelines (no teal per index.css line 12-13). Empty states are critical UX moments. The static gray icon feels lifeless and the off-brand button breaks visual consistency.
ui_ux_improvements.current_state: EmptyState.tsx line 15: SVG icon uses text-zinc-600 (gray). Line 32: CTA button uses 'from-sky-500 to-teal-500' which is NOT Anti-Slop compliant. No animation on the illustration. No aria-label for screen reader context.
ui_ux_improvements.proposed_change: Brand-align EmptyState: (1) Change icon color from text-zinc-600 to text-orange-400 on line 15 (2) Add animate-pulse-glow class (exists in index.css) to icon container (3) Change CTA button to 'from-orange-500 to-amber-500' (Anti-Slop compliant) (4) Add aria-label='No items found' to container div (5) Add role='status' for screen reader announcement (6) Consider using Lucide Sparkles icon for more visual interest. The animation should be subtle per prefers-reduced-motion.
ui_ux_improvements.user_benefit: Empty states feel intentional and on-brand rather than like an error. Users have clearer calls-to-action. Consistent color palette builds trust. Screen reader users understand the empty state context.

ui_ux_improvements.title: Add Keyboard Shortcut Hints to Tooltip-Worthy Buttons
ui_ux_improvements.description: Enhance button tooltips to include keyboard shortcut hints where shortcuts exist, improving discoverability of power user features.
ui_ux_improvements.rationale: The app has comprehensive keyboard shortcuts (useKeyboardShortcuts hook, KeyboardShortcutsModal) but they're hidden until users open the modal (?). Header.tsx buttons have title attributes but don't mention shortcuts. Power users discover shortcuts faster when hints are visible during normal use.
ui_ux_improvements.current_state: Header.tsx refresh button (line 82) has title='Refresh' with no shortcut hint. GenerativeSidebar.tsx has various action buttons without shortcut hints. The shortcuts object in App.tsx (lines 301-364) defines many shortcuts but they're not surfaced in UI tooltips. KeyboardShortcutsModal exists but requires explicit opening.
ui_ux_improvements.proposed_change: Add shortcut hints to tooltips: (1) Update Header refresh button: title='Refresh (Ctrl+R)' (2) Add to GenerativeSidebar generate button: title='Generate Background (Ctrl+Enter)' (3) Create helper: formatTooltip(label: string, shortcut?: string) => shortcut ? `${label} (${shortcut})` : label (4) Add data-shortcut attributes for potential future keyboard hint overlay (5) Consider subtle keyboard icon in button for discoverable shortcuts. Platform-aware: show Cmd on Mac, Ctrl on Windows.
ui_ux_improvements.user_benefit: Power users discover shortcuts naturally while using the app. Reduces time to learn advanced features. Users feel more productive as they adopt shortcuts. Creates perception of a thoughtfully designed professional tool.

ui_ux_improvements.title: Modal Close Button Touch Target Size
ui_ux_improvements.description: Add proper 44x44px minimum touch target to close buttons in SettingsModal and similar modals to meet iOS HIG and Android Material Design accessibility guidelines.
ui_ux_improvements.rationale: The close button in SettingsModal currently only displays an icon without a proper touch target wrapper. On mobile devices, small touch targets cause frustration and accessibility issues. The codebase already has touch-target utilities in index.css (line 357-365) and uses them in Toast.tsx close button, but they're not consistently applied to modal close buttons.
ui_ux_improvements.current_state: SettingsModal.tsx close button uses `absolute top-4 right-4 text-zinc-500 hover:text-white transition` with just an icon span, resulting in a touch target of approximately 24x24px (icon size only). Compare to Toast.tsx line 258-267 which properly uses `min-w-[44px] min-h-[44px]` for the close button.
ui_ux_improvements.proposed_change: Update the close button className to: `absolute top-4 right-4 min-w-[44px] min-h-[44px] flex items-center justify-center text-zinc-500 hover:text-white hover:bg-white/10 rounded-full transition focus-ring`. This matches the pattern already established in Toast.tsx and Header.tsx refresh button.
ui_ux_improvements.user_benefit: Easier to tap close button on mobile devices, better accessibility for users with motor impairments, consistent with other buttons in the app like Toast close button.

ui_ux_improvements.title: Custom Select Dropdown Arrow Indicator
ui_ux_improvements.description: Add a visible dropdown arrow indicator to all native select elements that have appearance-none styling, making it clear they are interactive dropdown menus.
ui_ux_improvements.rationale: The SettingsModal uses appearance-none on select elements to reset native styling, but doesn't add a custom dropdown arrow. This makes select fields visually indistinguishable from text inputs, causing confusion about their interactive nature. Users may not realize they can click to see options. The GenerativeSidebar model selector (lines 211-234) shows the correct pattern with an expand_more icon.
ui_ux_improvements.current_state: SettingsModal.tsx select elements (e.g., chat-model-select line 378-388, image-gen-model-select line 410-420) have `appearance-none` class but no visual indicator that they're dropdowns. The styling `w-full bg-zinc-950 border border-white/10 rounded-xl px-4 py-3 text-white text-xs font-medium focus-ring transition appearance-none` is identical to text inputs.
ui_ux_improvements.proposed_change:
Wrap each select in a relative div and add an absolute-positioned icon: `
expand_more
`. Add `pr-10` to select padding to avoid text overlap with icon.
ui_ux_improvements.user_benefit: Clear visual affordance that the element is a dropdown, consistent with UI conventions, reduced user confusion. Matches the pattern already used in GenerativeSidebar.

ui_ux_improvements.title: Toast Message Multi-line Support for Long Error Messages
ui_ux_improvements.description: Replace truncate class with line-clamp-2 for toast messages to prevent important error information from being cut off on smaller screens.
ui_ux_improvements.rationale: The Toast component uses `truncate` class (line 239) which cuts off longer messages with ellipsis. Combined with the `rounded-full` shape and uppercase tracking, important error messages or action confirmations may be illegible. Error messages especially need to be fully visible to help users understand what went wrong and take corrective action.
ui_ux_improvements.current_state: Toast.tsx line 239: message span has `text-[10px] sm:text-xs font-bold uppercase tracking-wider truncate flex-1` which truncates any text that doesn't fit in a single line. Messages like 'Voice: Failed to connect - check your API key in settings' would be cut off.
ui_ux_improvements.proposed_change: Replace `truncate` with `line-clamp-2` to allow 2 lines of text before truncating. Add `title={toast.message}` attribute for full text on hover. Consider changing container from `rounded-full` to `rounded-2xl` for messages exceeding 50 characters to better accommodate multi-line text.
ui_ux_improvements.user_benefit: Users can read complete error/success messages, especially important for error diagnostics and API key validation feedback. Reduces support requests from users who couldn't read the full error message.

ui_ux_improvements.title: Header Breadcrumb Context Display
ui_ux_improvements.description: Replace the empty center section in Header with contextual breadcrumbs or current location indicator when in Studio view.
ui_ux_improvements.rationale:
The Header component has an empty div (`
` at line 72-73) that takes up horizontal space but displays nothing. This creates visual imbalance and wastes valuable real estate that could help users understand their current location in the app, especially on larger screens.
ui_ux_improvements.current_state: Header.tsx line 72-73: Empty div between left (logo/back button/platform indicator) and right (refresh button) sections. The platformDisplay config exists and shows platform info, but no navigation context like current mode (Canvas, Templates, Media, LinkedIn).
ui_ux_improvements.proposed_change: Add a studioMode prop and display contextual breadcrumbs: `{onBackToDashboard && ({platformDisplay[activePlatform].name}/{studioMode})}`. Use subtle styling that doesn't compete with the platform indicator but provides additional context.
ui_ux_improvements.user_benefit: Users always know where they are in the app. Improved navigation understanding on larger screens. Better use of screen real estate. Reduces cognitive load when switching between modes.

ui_ux_improvements.title: Add Loading State Feedback to API Key Test Buttons
ui_ux_improvements.description: Enhance the API key test buttons in SettingsModal with proper loading spinners and disabled state handling during connection tests.
ui_ux_improvements.rationale: The SettingsModal has 'Test Connection' buttons for OpenRouter, OpenAI, and Replicate APIs (lines 349-355, 501-508, 546-555). While there's status tracking, the button text changes but lacks a visual spinner during the 'testing' state. Users may click multiple times thinking nothing is happening.
ui_ux_improvements.current_state: SettingsModal.tsx test buttons show 'Testing...' text when openRouterStatus === 'testing' (line 353) but use text-only feedback. The save button (lines 608-627) correctly shows a spinner (`sync`) during isSaving, but test buttons don't follow this pattern.
ui_ux_improvements.proposed_change: Update test buttons to match the save button pattern: `{openRouterStatus === 'testing' ? (<>syncTesting...) : 'Test Connection'}`. Also add `pointer-events-none` during testing to prevent double-clicks. The ConnectionStatus component shows status after, but inline feedback during is important.
ui_ux_improvements.user_benefit: Clear visual feedback that the connection test is in progress. Prevents accidental double-clicks that might trigger duplicate API calls. Consistent with save button behavior. Creates a more polished, responsive feel.
